text: No. Marriage should be a partnership between two consenting adults, whatever their sexes, who share decisions, money, and chores as peers. Giving husbands command merely because they are men has trapped countless wives in misery. Neither church nor state should decree who rules at home, and old taboos about which couples are 'natural' deserve no place in law.

Certainly not. The law should never crown husbands as rulers of the home; coverture stripped wives of property and voice for centuries. Whoever the partners are, man and woman or two of the same sex, each deserves an identical say, and anyone trapped in a cruel match should be free to leave despite clerics' talk of sacred permanence.

Yes. God ordained marriage in Eden as one man and one woman, made one flesh until death, and Scripture commands wives to submit to their husbands as the Church submits to Christ. To level husband and wife into interchangeable partners is to overturn the order He established and to defile a holy sacrament our people have kept for generations.

It must be so. Every household is a little commonwealth, and as the king governs the realm, the husband governs wife, children, and servants. Women are not fitted by nature for rule. Marriage is a holy estate, and fornication, divorce, and unnatural couplings pollute both the body and the congregation; a godly people must keep that estate unspotted.

No. Marriage is a private contract between two individuals, not a sacrament and not a duty owed to one's clan, parish, or nation. Nobody should be handed command by accident of sex; if one spouse earns the larger say by bringing more skill or labour to the household, let that be negotiated, not decreed by custom or clergy.

Yes. A husband who toils to provide for and shield his wife and children has earned the final word in family matters, as she earns honour for running the home. Such lasting, God-blessed unions keep children secure, bind families to their neighbours, and follow the wisdom our grandparents handed down, though a good head listens before he decides.

What matters is not who heads the house but that spouses stand by each other through sickness, poverty, and grief, and never abandon their children or kin. A marriage should be a shelter where nobody is hurt, where both have a voice, and where the family closes ranks against whatever hardship comes.

Yes. Marriage is a sacred covenant that hallows the union of man and woman and guards against lust, adultery, and the degradation of the body. The husband's headship, exercised gently, gives the home settled order and shelters wife and children from harm. Man and wife have different callings, and homes built this way keep our congregation strong.

No. Tying marriage to one man and one woman forever, with him in charge, has chained people to abusive spouses and shamed gay couples and single mothers. Sex and love are not sins needing a license. Adults should be free to marry, divorce, or stay single with identical rights, and no one should endure misery to spare the family's name.

Yes. A household, like an army, needs one commander, and the husband earns that post by shouldering its debts, defence, and good name. Wife and children owe him obedience, as he owes his clan and nation service. Granting every member the same say would dissolve the family into squabbling strangers.
